The Jones Act domestic lanes and the expedited service give a structurally higher base than before 2020.

The sustainable margin lies between the two and below the 2026 peak, so I fade margins from about 0.176 in 2026 toward 0.125.

growth_thesis.basis: Capacity and schedule are stated in the 10-K (March 2026). Whether the schedule still holds in November 2026 is not stated in the packet.
growth_thesis.claim: The fleet renewal program is the stated capacity driver for China. Three new Aloha Class vessels are due Q1 2027 to Q2 2028. Each is expected to add about 500 containers per voyage in the China service, about 15,000 containers per year in total. This requires on-time delivery and continued funding of milestone payments. Funding comes from the Capital Construction Fund (298.6 (table in millions), down from 532.7), cash, operating cash flow and available borrowings.
quotes: Each new vessel is expected to provide approximately 500 containers of additional capacity per voyage in the China service, representing an annual capacity increase of approximately 15,000 containers.

growth_thesis.basis: Volume changes and the case dismissal are stated in the cited items. Their role as a stable base is inferred from management's description.
growth_thesis.claim: The domestic Hawaii, Alaska and Guam tradelanes are a stable base rather than a growth source. Hawaii third-quarter volume fell 0.3% and Alaska fell 4.8%, while Guam rose 4.3%. Continued stability requires steady local economies and the Jones Act protection under which the company operates. The lawsuit challenging the Jones Act was dismissed.
quotes: In our domestic ocean tradelanes and logistics, we saw stable performance.
the case was dismissed on January 20, 2026.
